weakness.title: Insufficient Retention of Logs and Recordings
weakness.description: Access logs and recordings are kept for too short a period, so they are no longer available when an incident is discovered or investigated.

extended_description.applicability: Access control records, visitor registers, key logs and video recordings. Includes automatic overwriting of storage, retention periods set only by storage capacity, and records that are kept for a period shorter than the time an incident usually takes to be discovered.
extended_description.exploitation: An unauthorized or abusive access is discovered after the records covering it have been deleted or overwritten.

row.details: Incidents cannot be reconstructed, scoped or proven because the records no longer exist.
Past access cannot be examined to determine whether an earlier compromise took place.

row.description: Define a period for each type of record, based on the time incidents usually take to be discovered and on applicable law.
Provide enough capacity to hold the full retention period without early overwriting.
Suspend deletion for records related to an incident or an investigation until it is closed.

row.measure: Delete at the end of the period
row.description: Delete records once the period has ended, using a controlled and documented process.
Retention is limited by law. Retention periods must not exceed what applicable law allows, and recordings of individuals are often subject to shorter limits.

row.reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access
ISO/IEC 27001:2022, Annex A: 7.4 Physical security monitoring
